symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled units.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: The unsigned radius from a boundary point used to index an exact-distance regression.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The H\"older order of the bivariate potential-outcome regressions, with \(q\geq1\).

symbols.name: \iota
symbols.def: The order of the smooth embedded assignment-boundary chart, with \(\iota\geq1\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A fixed envelope for support size, score density, outcome smoothness, and moments.

symbols.name: c_{-}
symbols.def: The fixed lower constant for arm-specific probability mass in boundary balls.

symbols.name: r_0
symbols.def: The largest radius on which two-sided design thickness is imposed.

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A fixed fraction trimming the endpoints of a smooth boundary chart.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observed score that determines treatment through a known assignment partition.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A law for the potential outcomes, score, assignment, and observed outcome.

symbols.name: \mathcal{A}_{0,P}
symbols.def: The relatively closed score region assigned to control under \(P\), up to the boundary convention.

symbols.name: \mathcal{A}_{1,P}
symbols.def: The relatively closed score region assigned to treatment under \(P\), up to the boundary convention.

symbols.name: g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}
symbols.def: The canonical representative constructed in \(\mathrm{def:canonical\text{-}distance\text{-}regression}\), equal to the circle-integral ratio when its denominator is positive and to the H\"older representative \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) on zero-denominator radii and at the origin.

symbols.name: \widehat{\tau}_n
symbols.def: A generic estimator whose value at \(x\) may use only \(U_{n,P}(x)\).

symbols.name: \widetilde{\tau}_n
symbols.def: A generic estimator whose boundary curve may use the full sample \(O_{1:n}\) and the known assignment geometry jointly.

symbols.name: \gamma_P
symbols.def: An injective parameterization of a smooth assignment boundary.

symbols.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}
symbols.def: The difference of the two arm-specific degree-zero triangular-kernel intercepts constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}
symbols.def: The primitive two-sided-thickness class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:rectifiable\text{-}class}\); the stable symbol name no longer denotes a rectifiability premise.

symbols.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}
symbols.def: The endpoint-trimmed smooth-geometry class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:smooth\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{straight}}
symbols.def: The canonical two-half-plane subclass constructed in \(\mathrm{def:straight\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{C})
symbols.def: The trimmed distance risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:trimmed\text{-}distance\text{-}risk}\).

symbols.name: R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal{C})
symbols.def: The trimmed full-location risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:trimmed\text{-}location\text{-}risk}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}
symbols.def: The coarea and adversarial-density handle constructed in \(\mathrm{def:angular\text{-}density\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: The degree parameter for the order-\(m\) normalized-coarea remainder and the associated degree-\((m-1)\) local-polynomial rule.

symbols.name: \widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
symbols.def: The arm-intercept difference constructed in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), with its cutoff constant suppressed from the notation.

symbols.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{coarea}}
symbols.def: The thickness-free baseline coarea class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:radial\text{-}coarea\text{-}ambient\text{-}class}\).

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\mathcal{A}_{0,P},\mathcal{A}_{1,P}\) is a measurable partition of \(\mathcal{X}_P\) up to the boundary convention, and \(\mathcal{B}_P\) is its common relative interface.

standard.name: continuous random-design density without a common modulus
random-design density bounded away from zero and infinity
conditional variance bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(P\{X\in\mathcal{A}_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}\geq c_{-}r^2\) for every \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<r\leq r_0\).

novel.justification: This inspectable condition holds when the score density is bounded below and both assignment arms satisfy a uniform interior-cone or corkscrew condition at the known boundary, including smooth or polygonal geographic and administrative partitions whose opening angles stay away from zero. It excludes cusps, vanishing wedges, and arms that pinch out. The condition defines the primitive subclass and is load-bearing for both separated boundary packings and stable local estimation.

The novel tag records provenance only because the schema requires a standard-or-novel classification; this routine quantitative uniform geometric regularity restriction is not claimed as an original contribution. An injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) embedding covers smooth non-self-intersecting boundaries represented by geographic-information-system or spline charts, and it defines the smooth subclass and its trimmed chart.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal{X}_P=[-1,1]^2\), \(\gamma_P(u)=(2u-1,0)\), \(\mathcal{A}_{0,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2<0\}\), and \(\mathcal{A}_{1,P}=\{z\in\mathcal{X}_P:z_2\geq0\}\), with the displayed convention on the interface.

definitions.name: g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), define the canonical exact-distance regression on \([0,\infty)\) by \[g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\begin{cases}N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s=0,\\ \mu_{t,P}(x),&s>0\text{ and }Q_{t,P,x}(s)=0.\end{cases}\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}(q,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: K_\triangle
definitions.construction: \[K_\triangle(u)=\max\{1-|u|,0\}.\] This fixed kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, Lipschitz, supported on \([-1,1]\), and positive on \((-1,1)\).

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}
\mathfrak{H}_{\mathrm{ang}}
definitions.construction: Coarea angular-density confounding handle: expand each arm-specific radial conditional mean as a ratio of circle-level angular integrals; vary bounded continuous score densities through shrinking-scale angular imbalances while preserving the fixed radial mass envelope; pair those imbalances with disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines and bounded or Bernoulli outcomes; and use the induced compressed likelihoods to determine both a separated-center packing and the primitive regularity that prevents such confounding.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction:
Fix an integer \(m\geq1\), a cutoff constant \(c>0\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Put \(v_m(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^{m-1})^\top\), let \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), and set \(S_{P,x,i}=|D_{P,x,i}|\).  At the probability-zero value \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), assign the observation to neither arm.  Define
\[
 \widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)
 =\frac1{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{(2t-1)D_{P,x,i}>0\}
 K_\triangle(S_{P,x,i}/h)
 v_m(S_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
Let
\[
 G_m=\int_0^1uK_\triangle(u)v_m(u)v_m(u)^\top\,du,
 \qquad \lambda_m(c)=c\lambda_{\min}(G_m),
\]
and define the stabilized arm intercept and arm difference by
\[
 \widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)
 =\begin{cases}
 e_1^\top\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}
 \widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h),
 &\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}\geq\lambda_m(c)/2,\\
 0,&\lambda_{\min}\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}<\lambda_m(c)/2,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{1,h,c}(x)
 -\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{0,h,c}(x).
\]
The cutoff input \(c\) is suppressed from the notation for \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\).  The formula is defined for every \(h>0\); in an order-\(m\) coarea class it is used with \(c=\underline c\) and \(0<h\leq r_*\).  The strict sign convention, eigenvalue cutoff, inverse branch, and zero branch make this a pointwise Borel formula of \(U_{n,P}(x)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{coarea}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)=\left\{P:\text{for every }n\in\mathbb N,\text{ all member properties enumerated below hold}\right\}.\]

statements.justification: The bounded density supplies the upper half of local mass control, so the class needs only the primitive lower-thickness condition.
statements.gap: This is a supporting consequence of the density envelope rather than an additional Ahlfors-type premise.
statements.consumer: The local-constant stochastic bound and its population denominator use this estimate uniformly over boundary points.

statements.statement: For the fixed kernel \(K_\triangle\), there is \(\kappa_0=\kappa_0(c_{-},r_0)>0\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(h\), \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_P}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0,\qquad \inf_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}}\inf_{t\in\{0,1\}}\inf_{x\in\mathcal{B}_{P,\delta}}\Psi^{(0)}_{t,P,x}(h)\geq\kappa_0.\]
statements.justification: This theorem-local support verifies denominator stability for the one fixed degree-zero estimator used in both distance upper bounds.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance uses a broader high-level Gram condition for local-polynomial upper theory; this lemma derives only the scalar bound needed by the fixed triangular local-constant estimator.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable and smooth distance upper bounds use the same stable estimator without quantifying over kernels or polynomial degrees.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}}\cup\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}}\), \(x\in\mathcal{B}_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), coarea gives, for \(0<r\leq r_0\), \[P\{X\in\mathcal{A}_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=\int_0^r Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds\geq c_{-}r^2.\] Hence the set \(\{s>0:Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\}\) accumulates at zero, without requiring positivity at every radius. For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), \(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=N_{t,P,x}(s)/Q_{t,P,x}(s)\) is a version of \(\mathbb{E}_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]\). The canonical values on zero-denominator radii satisfy \[|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq Ls,\qquad s\geq0,\] and therefore \[\tau_P(x)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\bigl(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\bigr).\]
statements.justification: The lemma makes exact-distance conditioning well posed without asserting that every circle has positive arm density and shows that the canonical representative identifies the boundary contrast.
statements.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Theorem 1, supplies the identification background; this supporting lemma makes the coarea version and its behavior on zero-denominator radii explicit for the present primitive classes.
statements.consumer: The two distance-only frontier theorems use this canonical radial regression for their bias calculations and causal interpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a displayed law \(P\), boundary point \(x\), and arm \(t\), and put \(A_t=\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P\).  The map \(z\mapsto\lVert z-x\rVert_2\) is Lipschitz and has gradient of norm one away from the Lebesgue-null singleton \(\{x\}\).  The polar coarea formula and the density of \(X\) therefore give, for every \(r>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{X\in A_t\cap B_2(x,r)\}
 &=\int_0^r\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap A_t}
 f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)\,ds\\
 &=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(0<r\leq r_0\), two-sided thickness bounds the last expression below by \(c_-r^2\).  If \(Q_{t,P,x}=0\) almost everywhere on some \((0,r)\), its nonnegative integral there would be zero, a contradiction.  Thus every neighborhood of zero contains a positive-denominator radius; positivity at every radius is neither used nor concluded.

Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\).  Hence \(D_{P,x}\neq0\) almost surely, and deterministic assignment makes its sign equal to \(2T-1\).  For any bounded Borel \(a:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), consistency and the definition of \(\mu_{t,P}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(\lVert X-x\rVert_2)\right]
 &=\int_{A_t}a(\lVert z-x\rVert_2)\mu_{t,P}(z)f_P(z)\,dz\\
 &=\int_0^\infty a(s)N_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds,
\end{aligned}
\]
whereas the same calculation with \(Y\) replaced by one gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(\lVert X-x\rVert_2)\right]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation therefore permits the version
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) for which \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\).  Division occurs only on that set.

Because \(q\geq1\), the stated H\"older ball supplies
\[
 |\mu_{t,P}(z)-\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq L\lVert z-x\rVert_2.
\]
When \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\), the ratio \(N/Q\) is an \(f_P\,d\mathcal H^1\)-weighted average over points at distance \(s\), and hence
\[
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \leq\frac{\int Ls f_P\,d\mathcal H^1}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}=Ls.
\]
At \(s=0\), and at every positive zero-denominator radius, the canonical definition sets \(g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\mu_{t,P}(x)\), so the same inequality holds for every \(s\geq0\).  Therefore
\[
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)=\mu_{t,P}(x).
\]
Subtracting the two arm limits and using the separately defined causal target yields
\[
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}\{g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{1,P,x}(s)-g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{0,P,x}(s)\}
 =\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)=\tau_P(x).
\]
Thus the observed radial functional identifies, rather than defines, the causal contrast.

statements.statement:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on the law-class parameters and \(\delta\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), one can construct \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) centers on a trimmed straight boundary, separated by a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), and a finite hypercube family of laws in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\cap\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).  The assignment interface is straight; the regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines; every \(f_P\) is continuous and stays within the fixed density envelope; and the variance, tail, and arm-specific local-mass constants are common.  If two vertices differ only in the coordinate attached to a center \(x_j\), their target curves differ by at least \(c_1a_n\) at \(x_j\), both arm-specific radial mass densities at \(x_j\) agree at every radius, their arm-specific radial laws at \(x_j\) agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathbb Q_{n,P_\omega,x_j},\mathbb Q_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}},x_j}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
The perturbations use \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\), and the density envelope and arm-specific local-mass bounds hold uniformly over the whole hypercube.  If \(L>4\), the construction may be made on the canonical square, in which case the entire family also lies in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\).
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the narrowed statement and check all support, geometric, positivity, moment, and division conditions.

First use the unit square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), the lower and upper half-square assignment regions, and the interface
\[
\mathcal B=\{(u-1/2,0):0\leq u\leq1\},
\qquad \gamma(u)=(u-1/2,0).
\]
The base score density is \(f_*=1\).  The chart has length one, speed one, all derivatives of order at least two equal to zero, and \(C^{\iota+2}\)-norm at most one.  The line segment is closed and convex, hence every point in the plane has a unique metric projection onto it and its reach is infinite.  Thus the length, speed, derivative, and reach requirements hold for every \(L\geq4\), \(\iota\geq1\), and \(\rho_0>0\).  At an endpoint, the intersection of an arm and a sufficiently small boundary ball contains a quarter disk.  Since all densities constructed below are at least \(3/4\), for \(r\leq r_0\leq1/4\) each arm has mass at least \(3\pi r^2/16\), which exceeds \(c_{-}r^2\) because \(c_{-}\leq1/(16L)\).  Compact support and the assignment-partition conditions are immediate.

Choose a nonnegative radial \(C^\infty\) function \(\phi\), supported in the open unit disk, with \(\phi(0)=1\).  Put
\[
\Delta=d a_n,
\qquad
w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q},
\]
where the fixed constants are selected below.  Pack the interval \(\gamma([\delta,1-\delta])\) by centers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) separated by at least \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the disks \(B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint and contained in the unit square at a positive distance from the chart endpoints, and elementary interval packing gives
\[
M\geq c w^{-1}\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}.
\]
Let \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).  For every derivative order \(k\leq q\),
\[
\lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
\leq C_\phi\Delta w^{-k}
\leq C_\phi d_1^{-1}.
\]
Since the supports are disjoint, the same bound holds for every signed sum.  Taking \(d_1\) sufficiently large and the fixed affine slope \(b>0\) sufficiently small therefore puts all regressions below in the prescribed \(q\)-H\"older ball.

For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), define
\[
p_{0,\omega}(z)=\frac12,
\qquad
p_{1,\omega}(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
After decreasing \(b\) and \(d\), these functions take values in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Conditional on \(X=z\), take independent variables
\[
Y(t)=B_t+\varepsilon_t,
\qquad
B_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{t,\omega}(z)),
\qquad
\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,1).
\]
Then \(\mu_{t,P_\omega}=p_{t,\omega}\) and
\(1\leq\sigma^2_{t,P_\omega}\leq5/4\), which lies in \([L^{-1},L]\).  Hoeffding's lemma and the Gaussian moment-generating identity give
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[e^{\lambda\{Y(t)-p_{t,\omega}(X)\}}\mid X\right]
\leq e^{\lambda^2/8}e^{\lambda^2/2}
\leq e^{L^2\lambda^2/2},
\]
so the tail condition is uniform.

It remains to hide each regression bump in the radial experiment at its own center.  In polar coordinates \(z=x_j+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), take a continuous cutoff \(\chi\) satisfying \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\) and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\), and set
\[
A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\phi(r/w)}{br}\,
\chi\!\left(\frac{br}{8\Delta}\right).
\]
There is no division at zero because the cutoff is identically zero on a neighborhood of zero.  On its active region \(br\geq8\Delta\), \(\lvert A_n(r)\rvert\leq1/4\), and smooth compact support of \(\phi\) makes the correction continuous at the outer edge.  Because the disks are disjoint, the formula
\[
f_\omega(z)=1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_jA_n(\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2)
\frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2}
\mathbf 1\{z\in B_2(x_j,w)\}
\]
is unambiguous, with the summand defined as zero at \(x_j\).  Its angular correction integrates to zero on every full circle, so \(\int_Sf_\omega=1\); it is continuous and belongs to \([3/4,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).

Now compare adjacent vertices \(\omega\) and \(\omega^{(j)}\).  On either half-circle centered at \(x_j\), \(\int\cos\theta\,d\theta=0\).  Hence both arm-specific radial mass densities agree at \(x_j\) at every radius.  On the treated upper half-circle, whenever \(br\geq16\Delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega}(x_j+r e_\theta)\{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
-\int_0^\pi p_{1,\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+r e_\theta)\,d\theta\\
&\qquad=\pi\Delta\phi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r)=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
after orienting the adjacent pair so that \(\omega_j=1\).  The control equality follows from its constant regression.  A Bernoulli variable followed by the common Gaussian channel is determined, after angular mixing at a fixed radius, by the averaged Bernoulli success probability.  Thus the entire arm-specific radial laws agree outside \(r\leq16\Delta/b\), not only their conditional means.

Inside this radius, the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), all Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their radially averaged success probabilities differ by at most \(C\Delta\).  The inequalities \(\log u\leq u-1\) and data processing through the common Gaussian channel give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p,p')\leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(B+\varepsilon,B'+\varepsilon)\leq\operatorname{kl}(p,p').
\]
Consequently one compressed observation satisfies
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega,x_j},P^{\mathrm{dist}}_{\omega^{(j)},x_j})
\leq C\int_0^{16\Delta/b}\Delta^2r\,dr
\leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
Tensorization gives \(C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n\).  Moreover
\[
\log M=\left(\frac{1}{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choosing \(d\) sufficiently small gives the asserted bound for a fixed \(\alpha<1/8\), with enough slack that Poissonization at mean \(2n\) still has exponent below \(1/4\).  At \(x_j\), the adjacent target curves differ by \(\Delta\phi_j(x_j)=d a_n\), so \(c_1=d\).  The global density bounds already proved, together with the fixed half-square geometry, give common upper and lower arm-mass envelopes over the entire hypercube.  This completes membership in both \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rect}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}}\).

For the canonical square \([-1,1]^2\), use the required chart \(\gamma(u)=(2u-1,0)\) and base density \(f_*=1/4\).  When \(L>4\), let \(\varepsilon_L=1-4/L>0\), replace the cutoff constant \(8\) by a constant \(C_L\geq4/\varepsilon_L\), and choose \(d_1\) sufficiently large and then \(d/b\) sufficiently small as functions of \(L\).  The first choice keeps the cancellation region inside every bump also when \(q=1\); the second keeps its radius and all bump disks away from the trimmed endpoints for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The relative density perturbation is then at most \(\varepsilon_L/2\), so
\[
L^{-1}\leq\frac14(1-\varepsilon_L/2)\leq f_\omega
\leq\frac14(1+\varepsilon_L/2)\leq L.
\]
The cancellation and divergence calculations are unchanged up to constants depending on \(L\).  This verifies the canonical-square clause for \(L>4\).  At \(L=4\), the lower envelope \(f\geq1/4\) on a square of area four and normalization force \(f\equiv1/4\), so no nonzero angular density perturbation is possible; no canonical-square claim is made in that boundary case.
statements.justification: This explicit compressed-experiment construction converts angular-density confounding into the logarithmic uniform lower bound even under a perfectly smooth interface and smooth outcome regressions.
statements.gap: The published pointwise converse does not distribute continuous angular-density perturbations over separated trimmed-boundary centers with a logarithmic divergence budget.
statements.consumer: The rectifiable, smooth, and strict-slack straight-class distance converses use this family together with the coordinatewise overlap argument.

statements.statement: For every \(q\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,L,c_{-},r_0\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{rect}}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{rect}}.\] The upper inequality is attained by the fixed degree-zero triangular-kernel estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\). The lower inequality is supplied by the separated compressed-experiment family in \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\). This theorem concerns the explicitly defined primitive two-sided-thickness class and asserts no inclusion in, or same-class tightening of, the nonparametric class in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the sharp logarithm-bearing uniform frontier for the project-defined primitive two-sided-thickness coordinatewise-distance experiment.
statements.gap: The published lower bound is pointwise in its packing architecture. This theorem obtains the logarithmic factor on a separate class and makes no class-inclusion claim.
statements.consumer: Distance-based boundary analyses receive a rate-sharp bandwidth and worst-case uniform error guarantee under an inspectable arm-mass condition.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), there exist constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}<\infty\), depending only on \(q,\iota,L,c_{-},r_0,\delta\), such that \[c_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{sm}})}{a_n}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm},\delta}.\] The upper inequality is attained by \(\widehat{\tau}^{\mathrm{LC}}_{n,h}\) with \(h\asymp a_n\) and uses only the first-order continuity implied by \(q\geq1\), arm-specific local mass, and the fixed triangular kernel. The lower inequality is attained by the straight-interface, compact-support hard family in the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\); its regressions are disjoint \(q\)-H\"older bump perturbations of affine baselines, and its bounded continuous score densities have no common modulus.
statements.justification: The theorem isolates the coordinatewise information bottleneck without quantitative chart geometry.
statements.gap: The published smooth-bias calculation is fixed-law and does not provide a class-uniform higher-order constant under only bounded continuity of the score density.
statements.consumer: Analysts with a smooth assignment map receive the stable degree-zero distance rule and its sharp uniform bandwidth.

statements.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\).  On the nonempty canonical class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\),
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
If \(L>4\), then
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp a_n,
\]
and the distance lower bound is direct from the canonical-square version of the narrowed \(\mathrm{lem:angular\text{-}density\text{-}packing}\).  If \(L=4\), then the density envelope and the fixed square support force \(f_P\equiv1/4\), and
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}})\asymp s_{n,q}.
\]
Consequently the distance and location exponents are strictly separated for \(q>1\) when \(L>4\), while they coincide when \(q=1\) and also throughout the no-density-slack boundary case \(L=4\).
statements.proof_tex:
We first establish the full-location rate.  On the trimmed straight interface, each arm contains a fixed half-ball about every target point for all sufficiently small bandwidths.  The density bounds make every scaled bivariate polynomial Gram matrix uniformly nonsingular.  Taylor expansion of a \(q\)-H\"older regression to order \(q-1\) gives bias at most \(Ch^q\).  Repeating the finite-mesh conditional sub-Gaussian argument from the rectifiable theorem, now with bivariate polynomial weights of fixed degree, gives stochastic error
\[
 C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{nh^2}}.
\]
Thus a full-location local-polynomial estimator with
\(h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(2q+2)}\) has risk at most \(Cs_{n,q}\).

For the matching lower bound, take the uniform score density and Gaussian-noised Bernoulli outcomes used in the packing proof, but perturb one treatment regression by one of \(M\asymp h^{-1}\) disjoint two-dimensional bumps of width \(h\) and height \(h^q\), centered along the trimmed interface.  Every law remains in the straight class.  For two such laws, the one-observation relative entropy is bounded by a constant times
\(h^{2q}h^2\), so the product relative entropy is at most \(Cnh^{2q+2}\).  With the displayed bandwidth this is at most a sufficiently small multiple of \(\log M\), after reducing the bump amplitude.  The elementary entropy proof of Fano's inequality is as follows: if \(J\) is uniform on the \(M\) alternatives and \(Z\) is the sample, then
\[
 I(J;Z)\leq M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 \leq\alpha\log M,
\]
whereas any decoder with error probability \(p_e\) satisfies
\(I(J;Z)\geq(1-p_e)\log M-\log2\).  Hence \(p_e\) is bounded away from zero.  Sup-norm accuracy smaller than half the bump height would decode \(J\), proving the lower bound \(cs_{n,q}\).  This lower bound applies even to the full-location class, and therefore also to the distance-only class.

Suppose now \(L>4\).  The local-constant upper argument gives the distance upper bound \(Ca_n\).  The canonical-square version of the narrowed angular packing is a subset of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{straight}}\), and its exact-recovery argument gives the lower bound \(ca_n\).

Finally suppose \(L=4\).  Since \(\mathcal X_P=[-1,1]^2\) has area four and \(f_P\geq1/4\),
\[
 1=\int_{[-1,1]^2}f_P(z)\,dz\geq1.
\]
Equality forces \(f_P=1/4\) almost everywhere, and continuity makes the equality pointwise.  For a trimmed boundary point and sufficiently small \(s\), each arm-specific half-circle lies inside the square, so \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)=\pi s/4\).  Taylor's formula for \(\mu_{t,P}\), integrated over that half-circle, gives coefficients \(b_{t,k,P}(x)\) such that
\[
 \left|g^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t,P,x}(s)-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{q-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq Cs^q.
\]
A degree-\((q-1)\) one-sided local polynomial in signed radius therefore has bias \(Ch^q\), denominator order \(nh^2\), and uniform stochastic term \(C\sqrt{\log n/(nh^2)}\).  Balancing gives the distance upper bound \(Cs_{n,q}\).  The full-location lower bound already proved transfers to the smaller distance decision class, so the distance lower bound is \(cs_{n,q}\).  This proves every asserted case and shows exactly why the frozen all-\(L\) distance claim required correction.
statements.justification: Holding geometry and the causal target fixed reveals the statistical price of releasing only one distance coordinate, and also identifies the no-density-slack exception.
statements.gap: The full-regressor benchmark and location-based boundary theory do not pair their rate with a direct distance-only angular-confounding converse on the identical straight class.
statements.consumer: A data steward can determine whether a distance-only release loses an exponent: it does for \(q>1\) only when \(L>4\), and it does not when \(L=4\).

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then the probability of at least one decoding error is at least \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by their sum and write their densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Generate the binary compressed experiment by first drawing an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(A_j=1\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\); on \(A_j=0\), draw it from the normalized residual measure corresponding to \(\Omega_j\).  Zero-mass cases may be assigned arbitrary kernels because their indicators then have probability zero.  Use independent indicators and seeds across \(j\).  Because all observation spaces are standard Borel, a regular conditional kernel for \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists; applying it reconstructs the original local experiment.  Independently draw the bit-independent ancillary \(Z_0\) from its fixed law.  The conditional product premise shows that this coupling preserves the joint law of the stated experiment.

Fix the ambiguity indicators, all non-bit seeds, and the bits outside the ambiguous coordinate set \(A=\{j:A_j=1\}\).  If \(A\neq\varnothing\), consider the configurations of \((\Omega_j:j\in A)\) on which every decoder is correct.  Two configurations that differ only at coordinate \(j\in A\) cannot both succeed: decoder \(j\) sees the same \(S_j\), the same \(Z_{-j}\), and the same \(Z_0\) at the two endpoints, so its output is unchanged while the correct bit is reversed.  The successful configurations therefore form an independent set in the \(|A|\)-dimensional hypercube.  Pairing vertices along any coordinate shows that this set has at most \(2^{|A|-1}\) elements.  The ambiguous bits remain uniform, so conditional exact-success probability is at most \(1/2\).  If \(A=\varnothing\), it is at most one.  Averaging proves
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\Pr(A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(A\neq\varnothing)
 =\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]

For the relative-entropy consequence, define the Hellinger affinity \(H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}\).  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}
 \leq\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}.
\]
Since \(1-\sqrt{1-u}\geq u/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}
 \geq\frac12M^{-\kappa}.
\]
Therefore \(\prod_j(1-\rho_j)\leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}=o(1)\), and the preceding exact-success bound implies an any-error probability at least \(1/2-o(1)\).

statements.statement:
For every integer \(m\geq1\), cutoff constant \(c>0\), bandwidth \(h>0\), law \(P\), and boundary point \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), the rule in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\) is a measurable function of \(U_{n,P}(x)\), and therefore its arm difference is an element of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\).  Moreover, on the active-cutoff branch,
\[
 \left|\widehat\mu^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{t,h,c}(x)\right|
 \leq
 \frac{2\sqrt m}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}h^{-2}
 \left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|\right),
\]
whereas on the failed-cutoff branch the arm intercept is exactly zero.
statements.proof_tex:
All coordinates in the construction are Borel functions of the pairs \((Y_i,D_{P,x,i})\): absolute value and the strict sign indicators are Borel, \(K_\triangle\) and \(v_m\) are continuous, finite sums and products are Borel, the minimum eigenvalue is continuous on the symmetric matrices, and matrix inversion is continuous on the invertible matrices.  The active branch is contained in the set on which the minimum eigenvalue is at least \(c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)/2>0\); the other branch is assigned the fixed value zero.  Thus the piecewise formula is Borel.  It uses only \(U_{n,P}(x)\), including the declared convention when \(D_{P,x,i}=0\), so the definition of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) gives admissibility.

On the active branch, the spectral cutoff gives
\[
 \left\|\{\widehat G^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq\frac{2}{c\lambda_{\min}(G_m)}.
\]
Because \(0\leq K_\triangle\leq1\) and \(\|v_m(u)\|_2\leq\sqrt m\) on \(0\leq u\leq1\),
\[
 \left\|\widehat r^{(m)}_{t,x}(h)\right\|_2
 \leq\frac{\sqrt m}{nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n|Y_i|.
\]
Multiplication by \(e_1^\top\), whose Euclidean norm is one, proves the displayed bound.  The failed-cutoff assertion is exactly the zero convention in the construction.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), polar coarea gives, for every \(r>0\),
\[
 P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
Absolute continuity gives \(P(X=x)=0\), so the sign of \(D_{P,x}\) recovers the treatment arm almost surely.  For Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]=\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}.
\]
If, on some \((0,r_*]\), both arm denominators are positive and each ratio converges to \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) as \(s\downarrow0\), then
\[
 \tau_P(x)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}\left\{\frac{N_{1,P,x}(s)}{Q_{1,P,x}(s)}-\frac{N_{0,P,x}(s)}{Q_{0,P,x}(s)}\right\}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and put
\[
 A_t=\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap\mathcal X_P,
 \qquad R_x=\lVert X-x\rVert_2.
\]
The density envelope gives an absolutely continuous score law supported on \(\mathcal X_P\).  Polar coordinates centered at \(x\) and Tonelli's theorem therefore yield, for every \(r>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{X\in\mathcal A_{t,P}\cap B_2(x,r)\}
 &=\int_{A_t\cap B_2(x,r)}f_P(z)\,dz\\
 &=\int_0^r\int_{\partial B_2(x,s)\cap A_t}
 f_P(z)\,d\mathcal H^1(z)\,ds\\
 &=\int_0^rQ_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\end{aligned}
\]
No positivity condition and no division is used in this identity.

Because a singleton has planar Lebesgue measure zero, \(P(X=x)=0\).  On \(\{X\neq x\}\), the signed-distance definition gives \(D_{P,x}=(2T-1)R_x\), so its sign recovers \(T\) almost surely.

For any bounded Borel \(a:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\), deterministic assignment, consistency, and the definition of \(\mu_{t,P}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 &=\int_{A_t}a(\lVert z-x\rVert_2)\mu_{t,P}(z)f_P(z)\,dz\\
 &=\int_0^\infty a(s)N_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\end{aligned}
\]
The same calculation with \(Y\) replaced by one gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf1\{T=t\}a(R_x)]
 =\int_0^\infty a(s)Q_{t,P,x}(s)\,ds.
\]
Thus, on the half-line of sign \(2t-1\), the outcome-weighted law of \(D_{P,x}\) has density \(N_{t,P,x}(s)\), whereas its probability law has density \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)\).  The Radon--Nikodym characterization of conditional expectation permits the version
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid D_{P,x}=(2t-1)s]
 =\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(s>0\) with positive denominator.  The version may be assigned arbitrarily when the denominator is zero.

Finally, under the stated positivity and convergence conditions on \((0,r_*]\), subtraction of the two limits gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}\left\{
 \frac{N_{1,P,x}(s)}{Q_{1,P,x}(s)}-
 \frac{N_{0,P,x}(s)}{Q_{0,P,x}(s)}\right\}
 &=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)\\
 &=\tau_P(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is an identification statement for the separately defined causal target.

statements.statement:
The operational sufficient condition for a faster coordinatewise-distance frontier is a joint coarea remainder of the density, regression, and boundary geometry.  Precisely, fix any integer \(m\geq1\), with ambient indices \(q\geq1\) and \(\iota\geq1\), and let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{coarea}}(q,\iota,L)\) be any subclass for which there are constants \(A<\infty\), \(r_*>0\), and \(0<\underline c\leq\overline c<\infty\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal C\), \(x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<s\leq r_*\),
\[
 \underline c s\leq Q_{t,P,x}(s)\leq\overline c s,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{N_{t,P,x}(s)}{Q_{t,P,x}(s)}-\mu_{t,P}(x)-\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}b_{t,k,P}(x)s^k\right|\leq As^m,
\]
where the coefficient functions are uniformly bounded over \(P,t,x,k\).  Let \(\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\) be the stabilized coordinatewise degree-\((m-1)\) estimator in \(\mathrm{def:stabilized\text{-}distance\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial}\), built with \(K_\triangle\) and the lower radial constant \(\underline c\).  With
\[
 h_n\asymp\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(2m+2)},
\]
this estimator belongs to \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{dist}}\) and satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_{P,\delta}}
 \left|\widehat\tau^{(m),\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
 \right]
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{n,\delta}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal C)
 \leq C\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{m/(2m+2)}.
\]
If \(m\geq q\) and \(\mathcal C\) contains, for every sufficiently large \(n\), the uniform-design straight-interface \(q\)-H\"older bump submodel of width \(h_n\) and height proportional to \(h_n^m\) constructed in the proof, then the reverse inequality holds and the displayed rate is exact.  No matching converse is asserted when \(m<q\).  Independently, every law class containing the shrinking angular-imbalance family generated by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{ang}}\) has coordinatewise-distance lower frontier \(ca_n\).  Thus the order-one upper rate is the first-order saturation rate when that hard family is contained, while every \(m\geq2\) yields the faster displayed upper rate; the matching contained-bump certificate applies for every fixed \(m\geq q\).

Finally, there exists a bounded positive continuous density on a square with a straight interface such that a locally constant regression gives \(N(s)/Q(s)\) equal to that constant at every sufficiently small radius, whereas the affine regression \(\mu(z)=z_1\) gives \(N(s)/Q(s)=s^{1+\alpha}/2\) on the treated half-circle for some \(0<\alpha<1\), and therefore fails an order-two polynomial remainder.  Hence density alone does not determine these examples' joint normalized-coarea remainder; no universal weakest-threshold impossibility is asserted.

sampling_model.design: A boundary discontinuity design with a known binary assignment partition of a compact bivariate score support.
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has probability mass at least \(c_{-}r^2\) in every boundary ball of radius \(r\) for \(0<r\leq r_0\); \(f_P\leq L\) yields the derived upper estimate \(\pi Lr^2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The score density is bounded and continuous but has no class-uniform derivative or continuity modulus. Exact-distance regressions use the canonical coarea ratio on positive-denominator radii and the H\"older regression representative on zero-denominator radii. Both distance upper bounds use the fixed triangular kernel and degree zero; the comparison experiment permits estimators to use full score locations jointly.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The identification theorem supplies the distance-based causal functional; the smooth-bias theorem is fixed-law; the published nonparametric converse has order \(n^{-1/4}\), and its discussion predicts a missing uniform logarithm.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The primitive two-sided-thickness frontier establishes the logarithmic order on a separate two-sided-thickness class, the smooth theorem proves first-order saturation without a common density modulus, and the coarea theorem proves the order-\(m\) upper rate for every fixed \(m\geq1\), with a matching contained-bump converse for every \(m\geq q\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The location-based method retains the bivariate score and motivates the full-location comparison experiment.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The straight-class theorem proves the full-location benchmark and compares it with distance-only rates separately for \(L>4\) and \(L=4\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Stone's global H\"older benchmark in dimension two has order \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The straight-class full-location theorem derives this order and shows that the distance order coincides with it at \(L=4\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Separated alternatives and multiple testing motivate logarithmic sup-norm converses under information restrictions.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present converse adds an explicit overlap-coupling direct-product certificate for coordinatewise distance decisions with cross-center ancillary data.

tldr: The coordinatewise distance experiment has a sharp first-order uniform frontier even when the assignment boundary and outcome regressions are arbitrarily smooth. On the primitive rectifiable class with an inspectable arm-specific two-sided design-thickness condition, \(R_n^{\mathrm{dist}}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rect}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/4}\). The same rate holds on the endpoint-trimmed smooth class because bounded continuous score densities have no common angular regularity modulus; a straight-boundary angular-density packing with affine regressions supplies the converse. On the identical straight geometry, full score locations recover \((\log n/n)^{q/(2q+2)}\), strictly faster for \(q>1\). A central open question asks which primitive density or angular-balance regularity produces a transition to a faster distance-only frontier.

project_justification.gap: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) pointwise-style lower bound over its stated nonparametric class, while the following discussion predicts that uniform estimation carries a logarithmic factor. Their Theorem 3(ii) is a fixed-law interior smooth-bias result and does not determine a class-uniform minimax rate when continuous score densities have no common modulus.
project_justification.niche: The coordinatewise distance release discards angular locations. A primitive two-sided design-thickness condition stabilizes local estimation and supplies separated boundary neighborhoods, while unrestricted shrinking-scale angular imbalance can keep the induced radial regression only first-order regular even on a straight boundary.
project_justification.fill: The rectifiable theorem establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon on its own transparent primitive class. The smooth saturation theorem shows that geometry alone does not improve that frontier, and the straight-class comparison isolates the lost information by proving the faster Stone exponent for the full-location experiment.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the anchor. Its Theorem 1 supplies distance-based BATEC identification as background; the present supporting coarea lemma fixes a canonical exact-distance conditional representative, including its values on zero-denominator radii, for the proposal's primitive classes. Its Theorem 6 proves an \(n^{-1/4}\) lower bound over a class defined by independent sampling, bounded continuous density on compact support, a rectifiable support boundary, H\"older regression, and bounded continuous variance; Assumption 2(iv)'s Gram condition is not a premise of that theorem. The discussion after Theorem 6 conjectures that the missing logarithm reflects the pointwise lower-bound construction. The rectifiable result here establishes that logarithmic phenomenon on a separately defined primitive two-sided-thickness class, with no asserted inclusion or transfer. Theorem 3(ii) of the same paper is a fixed-law interior two-intersection bias statement; its supplemental angular-integral differentiation does not supply a common higher-order bias constant over the present bounded continuous density envelope, and the saturation theorem does not challenge the published fixed-law result. CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Location supplies the full-location benchmark experiment, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Survey documents the applied prevalence of location- and distance-based boundary analyses. Stone1982OptimalGlobal supplies the classical bivariate sup-norm exponent recovered by the full-location risk on the straight subclass. ChenChristensen2018SupNorm informs the separated-alternative multiple-testing architecture but studies a different inverse-regression experiment. AamariAaronLevrard2021Boundary supplies background for positive reach and \(C^2\) embedded-manifold geometry and is the source for the positive-reach premise. It is not the source of the proposal's two-sided length envelope, injective \(C^{\iota+2}\) chart, uniform chart-derivative envelope, lower chart-speed bound, or arm-specific design-thickness condition.
technical_internal_limitation: The decision restriction is coordinatewise: \(\widehat{\tau}_n(x)\) may use \(U_{n,P}(x)\) but may not triangulate score locations from distances released at other boundary points. A joint multi-center release is a different experiment. Exact-radius conditionals are only determined almost everywhere: the canonical representative uses the coarea ratio where \(Q_{t,P,x}(s)>0\) and the existing H\"older representative \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\) otherwise. Two-sided thickness ensures only that positive-denominator radii accumulate at zero; it does not imply positivity at every radius. The angular-density packing must explicitly construct bounded continuous density perturbations whose imbalance varies at scale \(a_n\), verify common density, tail, variance, H\"older, assignment-partition, reach, and arm-mass constants, keep the straight geometry and affine regressions, and prove the stated compressed-law Kullback--Leibler and packing bounds. Rough density by itself is not a lower-bound proof. For fixed \(P\), the higher-order angular integrals in Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 3(ii), may be differentiable; the diagnostic point is only that no uniform derivative bound follows from this proposal's density envelope. The primitive class here and the anchor's nonparametric class are distinct, and no inclusion is asserted.
honest_scope: The theorem-level targets are rate equivalences, not exact asymptotic constants. Exact-distance conditional expectations are identified only up to null radial sets; the canonical coarea representative fills those radii with \(\mu_{t,P}(x)\), and H\"older continuity makes its boundary limit unique without assuming a positive circle denominator at every radius. The rectifiable result establishes the predicted logarithmic phenomenon only under the novel primitive two-sided design-thickness condition; the logarithmic frontier on the exact nonparametric class of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem 6, remains open. The smooth theorem concerns the fixed endpoint-trimmed target and uses no density modulus beyond continuity and fixed upper and lower bounds. Its lower bound has an explicit compressed-experiment construction obligation on a straight two-half-plane submodel with affine regressions. The full-location Stone exponent is stated only for the separately defined full-location decision class and is strictly faster than the distance exponent only when \(q>1\). The weakest empirically meaningful regularity producing a faster distance-only frontier is open.
